fields.title: Conclusion
fields.md:
1. One-sentence conclusion: Berkshire has changed from a 'company that just piles up cash' into one that deployed about $41.8 billion (formula, 1-3) in the nine months of 2026; the weak points of its earnings engine are insurance (GEICO loss ratio +5.2%p) and interest-rate sensitivity, and the current share price of $570.89 is justified only if BPS compounds at 10.3% per year (formula).
2. Five-line briefing
   - 3Q26 after-tax operating earnings of $12.71 billion (−5.8%); excluding the FX distortion, roughly flat ([3Q26 press release](https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/news/nov0726.pdf)).
   - Insurance underwriting −43% and investment income −14%; BNSF +19%, BHE +8%, manufacturing and services +12% (same source).
   - Share repurchases of $9.65 billion in 3Q and $14.41 billion in 9M; zero in 2025 ([3Q26 10-Q](https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/qtrly/3rdqtr26.pdf)).
   - Headline cash of $377.4 billion ($356.9 billion excluding unpaid Treasury purchases), 28.9% of total assets (same source, formula).
   - Buffett became Chairman Emeritus on 2026-09-18, Howard Buffett is Chairman, and Abel is CEO — the succession discount is not yet in the numbers ([AP/OPB](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/09/18/warren-buffett-berkshire-hathaway/)).
3. Three data points to check directly before the next issue
   - 3Q26 13F (2026-11-16, per the 45-day rule, formula) — security-level detail of 3Q buys and sells.
   - The company's definition of the GEICO combined ratio (10-K or IR inquiry) — to resolve the gap between 84.5% (Forbes report) and 91.4% (10-Q formula).
   - Primary-source basis for the roughly $2 billion of post-quarter repurchases (Reuters report as source) — to be confirmed in the 4Q26 10-K.
